claude.sample_unit: patients (test cases: 30 external validation, 30 different-scanner generalizability)

links.outcome: CTV segmentation accuracy of locally fine-tuned vs vendor pretrained model against clinical contours
links.effect: LFT improved CTV DSC by 11.406% (ExVal) and 9.340% (GenEva), reduced 95HD by 46.866% and 42.120%, and corrected VPM over-contouring (relative volume error 17.9% vs -1.3%); p<0.01.
links.quote: Specifically, the improvements of DSC mean values are 11.406% in ExVal and 9.340% in GenEva with statistical significance (p-value < 0.01).

links.outcome: Performance change when applied to patients scanned on a different CT simulator
links.effect: No performance degradation with a different CT simulator; LFT mean CTV DSC 0.879 (ExVal) vs 0.874 (GenEva); OAR metrics between scanners negligibly different.
links.quote: We did not identify performance degradation when LFT and VPM models were applied in the GenEva dataset.

links.effect: DSC mean values improved 11.406% in ExVal and 9.340% in GenEva; p-value < 0.01.
links.quote: Specifically, the improvements of DSC mean values are 11.406% in ExVal and 9.340% in GenEva with statistical significance (p-value < 0.01).

links.outcome: Pretrained model CTV volume accuracy locally
links.effect: VPM CTV volume was 720.304 ± 90.789 cm 3 versus GT 617.879 ± 110.506 cm 3 in ExVal; p-value < 0.05.
links.quote: The CTV volumes (mean ± std) predicted by VPM and LFT in ExVal are 720.304 ± 90.789 cm 3 and 606.443 ± 90.677 cm 3 respectively with the benchmark GT as 617.879 ± 110.506 cm 3 (p-value < 0.05).

links.effect: No performance degradation identified in GenEva; LFT CTV mean DSC = 0.879 in Exval /0.874 in GenEva.
links.quote: We did not identify performance degradation when LFT and VPM models were applied in the GenEva dataset.
